concepts.title: Building a total inside a loop
Returning a value from a function
Changing a property of an object

misconceptions.description: Believes a loop with a < condition also runs for the bound itself.
Believes the variable holds only the last value added, not the sum.
Counts the first pass through a loop as pass zero.
Reads the value a variable has at the end of the program for every earlier step.
Believes the first element of an array has index 1.
Believes assigning to a new property name changes an existing property.
Believes an object declared with const cannot have its properties changed.
Believes const has no effect at all when the value is an object.

conceptCard.title: Keeping a running total
conceptCard.body: A loop can build a result one step at a time. Declare the total before the loop, change it inside the loop, and read it after the loop ends. The loop condition decides which values take part.

conceptCard.title: Indexes start at zero
conceptCard.body: Every element of an array has a position called its index. The first index is 0, so the last index is always one less than the number of elements.

conceptCard.title: A function hands back a value
conceptCard.body: The return statement ends a function and sends a value back to the place that called it. The call itself then stands for that value, so it can be stored in a variable or printed.

conceptCard.title: Properties can be reassigned
conceptCard.body: An object keeps its values in named properties. Assigning to a property that exists replaces its value. Assigning to a name that does not exist yet adds a new property and leaves the others alone.

options.feedback: Right. The loop runs for 2, 3 and 4, and each pass adds that number to the total.

items.prompt: What value does stock hold right after line 4 has run for the second time?

options.feedback: Right. The first pass leaves 7 and the second pass takes 4 away from that.
That is the value after the first pass. The question asks about the second time line 4 runs.
That is the value when the program ends, after all three passes. After the second pass one amount is still waiting.

items.explanation: The loop visits the amounts in order. After the first pass stock is 10 - 3 = 7. After the second pass it is 7 - 4 = 3. The third pass has not happened yet at that moment.
hints: Follow line 4 once for every element of sold.
The variable keeps its value from one pass to the next.

items.prompt: Write the body of largest so that it returns the biggest number in the array numbers.
items.explanation: Start with the first element as the best so far, compare every element with it, and keep the larger one. Starting from the first element instead of 0 keeps the answer right when every number is negative.
hints: You need one variable that remembers the biggest number seen so far.
Compare each element with the remembered value and replace it when the element is larger.
Begin with the first element, loop over the array, and return the remembered value after the loop.

items.prompt: Line 2 changes a property of an object declared with const. Which statement explains what the program does?

options.text: const only stops pet from being assigned again; the object it holds can still change.
options.feedback: Right. The variable keeps pointing at the same object, and that object's property is updated, so the program prints 4.

options.text: The assignment on line 2 is ignored, so the program prints 3.
options.feedback: The program prints 4. const protects the variable, not the contents of the object it refers to.

options.text: const has no effect on objects, so pet could also be given a new object.
options.feedback: Assigning a new object to pet would throw an error. const still forbids reassigning the variable itself.

items.explanation: const fixes which value a variable refers to. Here that value is an object, and the object itself stays changeable. Line 2 updates a property of the same object, so line 3 prints the new age.
hints: Look at what stands on the left of the assignment on line 2.
Changing a property is different from assigning a new value to the variable.
Ask whether line 2 gives pet a different object or changes the one it already has.
